title: The Hubble Tension (Early vs Late Universe)
bottleneck: The CMB-calibrated expansion rate (67-68 km/s/Mpc) disagrees with local distance-ladder measurements (~73 km/s/Mpc) at 4-5 sigma, with DESI DR2 combinations keeping the tension at 3.6-4.2 sigma. Proposed fixes (early dark energy, extra relativistic species, local void) each solve part of the problem while worsening other fits, and no single solution commands consensus. Early-universe fixes like early dark energy ease the tension but are increasingly squeezed by large-scale structure data, while late-universe fixes struggle with supernova calibration.
why_it_blocks: A genuine tension means LambdaCDM is incomplete; resolving it likely requires new physics in the early or late universe.
current_state: JWST Cepheid re-observations largely confirm the local ladder; early-dark-energy models remain viable but increasingly constrained by CMB and large-scale structure. A resolution will likely require new physics plus better systematics control; neither alone currently suffices.
